questions.text:
The diagram shows the setup for a chemical reaction which produces a gas. The gas is then dried and collected.

[DIAGRAM – GAS COLLECTION APPARATUS]
A conical flask produces a gas. The gas passes through a drying tube containing calcium oxide (CaO). Dry gas is then collected. Labels: 'gas collected' and 'calcium oxide'.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

What could the gas be?

A  carbon dioxide
B  hydrogen
C  oxygen
D  sulfur dioxide

The melting and boiling points of the gases in a sample of air are shown.

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 3 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'gas', Column 2: 'melting point / °C', Column 3: 'boiling point / °C'
Row 1: oxygen | −219 | −183
Row 2: argon | −189 | −186
Row 3: nitrogen | −210 | −196
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

At which temperature will the sample of air contain oxygen as the only liquid?

A  −174 °C
B  −187 °C
C  −215 °C
D  −222 °C

Which of the following pairs of substances can be separated by heating?

A  ammonium chloride and iodine
B  ammonium chloride and potassium iodide
C  copper(II) nitrate and potassium iodide
D  copper(II) nitrate and sodium chloride

The following diagrams can be used to illustrate the following.

1  a mixture of elements and compounds
2  a mixture of elements
3  molecules of an element
4  molecules of a compound

[DIAGRAM – FOUR PARTICLE DIAGRAMS]
Four labelled boxes W, X, Y, Z showing different particle arrangements:
W: open circles of same size (same type, widely spaced).
X: two types of open circles of same size mixed (two types of elements).
Y: open squares and open circles (two different types — element molecules + compound molecules).
Z: mixed large solid circles and small open circles (two very different types — mixture with compound).
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

What is the correct order of the diagrams?

|   | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | Y | Z | X | W |
| B | Z | Y | X | W |
| C | Z | Y | W | X |
| D | Z | X | W | Y |

A student wrote the following statements in her test script:

Statement 1: 'Hydrogen chloride has a lower boiling point than calcium chloride as covalent bonds are weaker than electrostatic forces of attraction.'

Statement 2: 'In a gaseous sample of methane, the intermolecular forces of attraction between the CH₄ molecules are weak.'

Statement 3: 'In silicon dioxide, all valence electrons of silicon are used in the making of covalent bonds.'

Which of the above statements are correct?

A  statement 1 and statement 2
B  statement 1 and statement 3
C  statement 2 and statement 3
D  statement 1, 2 and 3

The table shows the proton number and nucleon number of elements M and N.

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 2 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'element', Column 2: 'proton number', Column 3: 'nucleon number'
Row 1: M | 13 | 27
Row 2: N | 8 | 16
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

When M and N react to form a compound, what will be the mass of one mole of the compound?

A  43
B  70
C  102
D  113

The relative masses and relative charges of particles V to Z are shown in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2 respectively.

[DIAGRAM – TWO BAR GRAPHS]
Fig. 1: Bar graph with y-axis 'relative mass' (0 to 4) and x-axis showing particles V, W, X, Y, Z. V and Z have relative mass ≈ 4; W and Y have relative mass ≈ 1; X has relative mass ≈ 0 (very small, near zero).
Fig. 2: Bar graph with y-axis 'relative charge' (−2 to +2) and x-axis V, W, X, Y, Z. V has charge +2; W has charge +1; X has charge near 0 (or −1, very small negative); Y has charge +1; Z has charge +2.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

Which of the following statements are correct?

1  W represents an electron.
2  X represents a hydrogen ion.
3  Z represents the nucleus of a helium atom.
4  V and Y represent the nuclei of isotopes.

A  1 and 2 only
B  2 and 3 only
C  1, 2 and 4 only
D  2, 3 and 4 only

Which statement best explains why brass, made of copper and zinc, is suitable to make music instruments compared to pure copper?

A  The zinc atoms form strong metallic bonds with copper atoms in brass.
B  The zinc atoms have more valence electrons than copper atoms.
C  The zinc atoms prevent layers of copper atoms from sliding over each other.
D  The zinc atoms prevent the 'sea of electrons' from moving freely.

A 286 g sample of hydrated copper(II) sulfate contains 126 g of water of crystallisation.

What is the correct formula of this compound?

A  CuSO₄·3H₂O
B  CuSO₄·5H₂O
C  CuSO₄·7H₂O
D  CuSO₄·9H₂O

Aqueous sodium hydroxide reacts with a certain metal chloride, MCl_n solution, according to the equation:

MCl_n + nNaOH → M(OH)_n + nNaCl

10.0 cm³ of 3.00 mol/dm³ NaOH solution were found to react with 10.0 cm³ of 1.50 mol/dm³ MCl_n solution.

What is the formula of the metal chloride?

A  MCl
B  MCl₂
C  MCl₃
D  MCl₄

Sulfur dioxide can react with oxygen to form sulfur trioxide as shown.

2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g)

If 200 cm³ of sulfur dioxide is reacted with 200 cm³ of oxygen, what is the volume of gases remaining after the reaction?

A  100 cm³
B  200 cm³
C  300 cm³
D  400 cm³

An aqueous solution has a pH of 14.

What does this imply about the concentration of ions present in the solution?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: row label, Column 2: 'concentration of OH⁻ ions', Column 3: 'concentration of H⁺ ions'
Row A: high | low
Row B: high | none
Row C: low | high
Row D: low | none
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  high OH⁻, low H⁺
B  high OH⁻, none H⁺
C  low OH⁻, high H⁺
D  low OH⁻, none H⁺

Which of the following equations suggests that the underlined oxide has amphoteric properties?

A  Ga₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaGaO₂ + H₂O
B  Li₂O + H₂O → 2LiOH
C  CuO + 2HCl → CuCl₂ + H₂O
D  Cl₂O + 2NaOH → 2NaClO + H₂O

Which of the following salts can be prepared using the same method?

A  calcium sulfate, zinc chloride
B  copper(II) sulfate, silver nitrate
C  potassium nitrate, magnesium nitrate
D  potassium iodide, silver iodide

The graph shows the optimal yield of ammonia at 450 °C and 250 atm.

[DIAGRAM – GRAPH AND COMPARISON GRAPHS]
Reference graph: y-axis 'yield of ammonia', x-axis 'time'. A single curve labelled '450 °C' rises and levels off at a plateau.
Four comparison graphs A, B, C, D each showing two curves (450 °C solid and 500 °C dashed) rising over time:
Graph A: 500 °C curve is higher and reaches plateau sooner than 450 °C.
Graph B: 450 °C reaches higher plateau; 500 °C starts slower but plateaus lower.
Graph C: Both plateau at same height; 450 °C rises faster.
Graph D: 500 °C rises faster but both reach same plateau.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

Which of the following graphs shows a correct comparison of the yield of ammonia produced at temperature of 500 °C and 250 atm?

A  Graph A
B  Graph B
C  Graph C
D  Graph D

Several tests are performed on an unlabelled bottle containing an aqueous sample.

Which of the following results is likely to correspond to iron(II) chloride?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 4 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: row label, Column 2: 'test 1: add dilute nitric acid, then aqueous silver nitrate', Column 3: 'test 2: add dilute nitric acid, then aqueous barium nitrate', Column 4: 'test 3: add aqueous sodium hydroxide dropwise, then add in excess'
Row A: no visible reaction | white precipitate formed | green precipitate formed, does not dissolve in excess sodium hydroxide
Row B: no visible reaction | white precipitate formed | reddish-brown precipitate formed, does not dissolve in excess sodium hydroxide
Row C: white precipitate formed | no visible reaction | green precipitate formed, does not dissolve in excess sodium hydroxide
Row D: white precipitate formed | no visible reaction | reddish-brown precipitate formed, does not dissolve in excess sodium hydroxide
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  Row A
B  Row B
C  Row C
D  Row D

Disproportionation is a reaction in which the same element is both oxidised and reduced.

Which reaction is not an example of disproportionation?

A  Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O
B  2CuCl → CuCl₂ + Cu
C  2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂
D  2Pb(NO₃)₂ → 2PbO + 4NO₂ + O₂

In an electrolysis experiment, the same amount of charge deposited 19.2 g of copper and 9 g of scandium. The charge on the copper ion is +2.
[A_r: Sc, 45; Cu, 64]

What was the charge on the scandium ion?

A  +1
B  +2
C  +3
D  +4

Which property is not typical of transition metals?

A  They exhibit variable oxidation states.
B  They form coloured compounds.
C  They have high melting points.
D  They have low densities.

The electrolysis set-up shown is incomplete.

[DIAGRAM – ELECTROLYSIS APPARATUS]
An electrolysis cell with two carbon electrodes dipping into concentrated hydrochloric acid. The box labelled X at the top shows where gas collection tubes should be placed above each electrode.
Four options A, B, C, D show different arrangements of gases (O₂ and H₂, or Cl₂ and H₂) above the two electrodes:
A: O₂ above left electrode, H₂ above right electrode.
B: Cl₂ above left electrode, H₂ above right electrode.
C: O₂ above left electrode, H₂ above right electrode (smaller volumes than A).
D: H₂ above left electrode, Cl₂ above right electrode.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

What should be shown at X when the solution has been electrolysed for some time?

A  O₂ and H₂
B  Cl₂ and H₂
C  O₂ and H₂ (smaller volumes)
D  H₂ and Cl₂

Lithium and rubidium are both in Group 1 of the Periodic Table.

Which statement is correct?

A  Lithium atoms and rubidium atoms have the same number of electrons in their outer shell.
B  Lithium atoms and rubidium ions have the same number of electrons in their outer shell.
C  Lithium atoms are larger than rubidium atoms.
D  Rubidium ions are larger than rubidium atoms.

In the following setup, magnesium and copper strips are pressed against a piece of wet filter paper soaked in dilute sulfuric acid and current can be detected by an ammeter.

[DIAGRAM – ELECTROCHEMICAL CELL]
A simple cell: a wet filter paper strip soaked in dilute sulfuric acid, with a copper strip on top and a magnesium strip below, connected externally by a wire to an ammeter. Labels: 'copper', 'wire', 'wet filter paper', 'magnesium'.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

Which of the following statements is correct?

A  Copper strip decreases in size.
B  Electrons flow from copper to magnesium through the external wire.
C  Magnesium strip is coated with a pink substance.
D  Oxidation occurs on the magnesium strip.

The graph shows the variation in boiling points for eight consecutive elements in Periods 3 and 4 of the Periodic Table with atomic numbers less than or equal to 20.

[DIAGRAM – LINE GRAPH]
A line graph. Y-axis: 'boiling point / °C'. X-axis: 'atomic number'. Eight points labelled P, Q, R, S, T, U, V, W in order of increasing atomic number. P is high, Q is the highest, R drops low, S is slightly higher than R, T drops to nearly zero (noble gas), U is very low, V rises again, W is the highest in Period 4. The graph zigzags showing the periodic trend.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

What can be deduced from the above?

A  Element P is a Group 1 element.
B  Element S has a metallic lattice structure.
C  Element U exists as diatomic molecules.
D  Element V is a strong reducing agent.

Magnesium blocks are attached to iron pipes to prevent them from rusting.

Which statement best explains how magnesium stops the iron from rusting?

A  Magnesium forms a compound with iron.
B  Magnesium reacts in preference to iron.
C  Magnesium reacts to form a protective coating of magnesium oxide on the iron.
D  Magnesium stops oxygen in the water from getting to the iron.

Three different reactions were set up as shown.

[DIAGRAM – THREE DISPLACEMENT REACTIONS]
Three beakers labelled 1, 2 and 3.
Beaker 1: metal Z dipped into aqueous nitrate of metal W.
Beaker 2: metal W dipped into aqueous nitrate of metal X.
Beaker 3: metal X dipped into aqueous nitrate of metal Y.

In beaker 1, metal W is displaced from solution.
In beaker 2, metal X is displaced from solution.
In beaker 3, metal Y is displaced from solution.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

What is the order of reactivity of these four metals?

|   | most reactive → | → | → | least reactive |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | W | X | Z | Y |
| B | X | Y | W | Z |
| C | Y | X | W | Z |
| D | Z | W | X | Y |

Limestone usually contains impurities.

The diagram shows the change in mass when pure calcium carbonate is heated.

Which graph, A, B, C or D, shows a sample of limestone, of the same mass, containing impurities that are thermally stable to decomposition?

[DIAGRAM – LINE GRAPH]
A line graph. Y-axis: 'change in mass / g' (negative values, mass decreasing). X-axis: 'time / min'. Four curves labelled A, B, C, D and one dashed curve labelled 'pure calcium carbonate' (curve B, intermediate). Curve A levels off at a smaller mass loss (above the dashed line). Curves C and D level off at greater mass loss (below the dashed line).
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

A  Curve A
B  Curve B
C  Curve C
D  Curve D

The reaction of a metal oxide with hydrogen is shown.

[DIAGRAM – REDUCTION APPARATUS AND TABLE]
A horizontal glass tube containing a metal oxide, heated by a Bunsen burner. Hydrogen gas passes through the tube. The gas exiting is burned (flame shown at right end of delivery tube).
A table with 2 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'metal oxide', Column 2: 'mass of metal oxide after heating'
Row A: copper(II) oxide | increases
Row B: lead(II) oxide | decreases
Row C: magnesium oxide | increases
Row D: zinc oxide | decreases
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

Which of the following is correct?

A  copper(II) oxide — mass increases
B  lead(II) oxide — mass decreases
C  magnesium oxide — mass increases
D  zinc oxide — mass decreases

Hydrogen and chlorine react together to form hydrogen chloride.

H₂(g) + Cl₂(g) → 2HCl(g)   ΔH = −92 kJ/mol

The average bond energies of two of the bonds involved are shown in the table.

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 2 columns and 1 row (excluding header).
Column 1: 'bond', Column 2: 'bond energy / kJ/mol'
Row 1: H–H | 436
Row 2: Cl–Cl | 244
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

What is the bond energy of a H–Cl bond?

A  294 kJ/mol
B  386 kJ/mol
C  588 kJ/mol
D  772 kJ/mol

Which change will increase the speed of the reaction between 1 mol of two reacting gases?

A  a decrease in temperature
B  a decrease in the volume of the reaction flask
C  a decrease in surface area of the catalyst
D  an increase in the volume of the reaction flask

A diagram for the energy change during a chemical reaction is shown.

[DIAGRAM – ENERGY PROFILE DIAGRAM]
An energy profile diagram. Y-axis: 'energy'. The reactants start at a higher energy level, the products end at a lower energy level. An arrow points downward from reactants to products level (exothermic).
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

For which reaction(s) would this be an appropriate diagram?

1  CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O
2  C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ → 6CO₂ + 6H₂O
3  2C + O₂ → 2CO

A  1 only
B  1 and 2 only
C  1 and 3 only
D  1, 2 and 3

In two separate experiments, the reaction of calcium carbonate with an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid was investigated. The calcium carbonate used in Experiment 1 was more finely divided than that used in Experiment 2.

Assuming all other conditions were identical in both experiments, which of the following graphs best illustrates the results?

[DIAGRAM – FOUR LINE GRAPHS]
Four graphs labelled A, B, C, D. Each shows two curves labelled '1' (experiment 1) and '2' (experiment 2). Y-axis: 'volume of CO₂ / cm³'. X-axis: 'time / s'.
Graph A: Curve 2 reaches a higher plateau than curve 1, both rise steeply.
Graph B: Curve 1 reaches a higher plateau than curve 2; curve 1 rises faster.
Graph C: Curve 1 rises faster and plateaus at the same level as curve 2.
Graph D: Curve 1 rises faster but plateaus at a lower level than curve 2.
Recommended rendering tool: image generator.

A  Graph A
B  Graph B
C  Graph C
D  Graph D

Solution X reacts with solid Y to form a gas.

Which two diagrams show suitable methods for investigating the speed of reaction?

[DIAGRAM – FOUR SETUPS]
Four labelled setups 1, 2, 3 and 4, each showing a conical flask containing solution X and solid Y on a balance.
Setup 1: flask sealed with a rubber stopper. Gas cannot escape. Balance records mass.
Setup 2: flask sealed with cotton wool plug. Gas can escape slowly. Balance records mass.
Setup 3: flask sealed with a rubber stopper connected to a gas syringe. Gas collected in syringe.
Setup 4: flask sealed with cotton wool plug connected to a gas syringe. Cotton wool lets gas escape before reaching syringe.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

A  1 and 3
B  1 and 4
C  2 and 3
D  2 and 4

The table shows the boiling points of four fractions, P, Q, R and S, obtained when crude oil is distilled.

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 2 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: 'fraction', Column 2: 'boiling range / °C'
Row P: 35–75
Row Q: 80–145
Row R: 150–250
Row S: greater than 250
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

How is fraction P different from S?

A  Fraction P is collected at the bottom while fraction S is collected at the top.
B  Fraction P is larger in molecular masses than fraction S.
C  Fraction P is more flammable than fraction S.
D  Fraction P is more viscous than fraction S.

What will propanol, C₃H₇OH, form on complete oxidation?

A  CH₃CO₂H
B  C₂H₅CO₂H
C  C₃H₇CO₂H
D  C₄H₉CO₂H

The compound C₆H₁₂ undergoes the following process.

C₆H₁₂ → ethene + compound Y

Which row in the table correctly identifies process X and compound Y?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: row label, Column 2: 'process X', Column 3: 'compound Y'
Row A: cracking | butane
Row B: cracking | butene
Row C: distillation | butane
Row D: distillation | butene
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  cracking — butane
B  cracking — butene
C  distillation — butane
D  distillation — butene

How many isomers are there for butan-2-ol?

[DIAGRAM – STRUCTURAL FORMULA]
The structural formula of butan-2-ol: a 4-carbon chain with an OH group on carbon 2.
H H H H
| | | |
H–C–C–C–C–H
| | | |
H OH H H
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

A  1
B  2
C  3
D  4

An ester with molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₂ undergoes hydrolysis to form an alcohol G and an acid H. Alcohol G can be oxidised to acid H by warming with acidified potassium manganate(VII).

Which of the following is the formula of the ester?

A  CH₃COOC₄H₉
B  C₂H₅COOC₃H₇
C  C₃H₇COOC₂H₅
D  HCOOC₅H₁₁

A compound has the following structure.

[DIAGRAM – STRUCTURAL FORMULA]
The displayed formula of prop-2-enoic acid (acrylic acid): CH₂=C–COOH
H H O
| | ‖
H–C=C–C–O–H
The molecule has a C=C double bond and a –COOH group.
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

Which reaction(s) will occur with this compound?

1  It will react with aqueous bromine under room temperature.
2  It will react with an alcohol to form an ester.
3  It will react with sodium metal.

A  1 only
B  1 and 2 only
C  2 and 3 only
D  1, 2 and 3

The diagram shows part of the molecule of polymer Q.

[DIAGRAM – POLYMER STRUCTURE]
A section of a polymer chain showing repeating amide linkages: –CO–C–N–CH₂–CH₂–N–CO–C–N–
The chain has alternating carbonyl groups (C=O) and nitrogen (NH) groups connected by –CH₂–CH₂– spacers. This is characteristic of a polyamide (nylon-like structure).
Recommended rendering tool: SVG.

Which row correctly describes the monomer of Q and how the polymer is formed?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: row label, Column 2: 'functional groups present in the monomer', Column 3: 'polymer formed by'
Row A: alkene and amine | addition polymerisation
Row B: alkene and amine | condensation polymerisation
Row C: carboxylic acid and amine | addition polymerisation
Row D: carboxylic acid and amine | condensation polymerisation
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  alkene and amine — addition polymerisation
B  alkene and amine — condensation polymerisation
C  carboxylic acid and amine — addition polymerisation
D  carboxylic acid and amine — condensation polymerisation

Which row in the table shows the correct atmospheric pollutant and its possible effects?

[DIAGRAM – TABLE]
A table with 3 columns and 4 rows (excluding header).
Column 1: row label, Column 2: 'pollutant', Column 3: 'effect'
Row A: CFCs | layer forms photochemical smog
Row B: CO₂ | is poisonous to humans
Row C: CO | cause depletion of the ozone
Row D: NO₂ | forms acid rain
Recommended rendering tool: SVG table.

A  CFCs — photochemical smog
B  CO₂ — poisonous to humans
C  CO — ozone depletion
D  NO₂ — acid rain
